claim: NVIDIA reports pretraining a 12B model on 10T tokens in NVFP4 with loss and downstream accuracy comparable to an FP8 baseline
Stable 4-bit pretraining required random Hadamard transforms, two-dimensional quantisation, stochastic rounding and selected higher-precision layers - the format alone is not enough
The NVFP4 paper's abstract page gives neither the benchmark scores nor the names of the layers held at higher precision
NVFP4's small group size provably neutralises traditional outlier-mitigation techniques, and MXFP4's power-of-two scales induce high error
MR-GPTQ kernels reach up to 3.6x layer-wise and 2.2x end-to-end on a B200 and 6x / 4x on an RTX 5090, against an FP16 baseline whose tuning the abstract does not state
FP4 is not an automatic upgrade over INT4; format-specialised methods are what open the trade-off

An LLM agent generating low-level GPU kernel code was a 0.40x geomean regression against PyTorch on 59 KernelBench problems; a CUTLASS-backed DSL raised it to 1.27x and speed-of-light guidance to 1.56x
That paper's abstract does not state whether the PyTorch baseline was eager or compiled, nor which GPU was used
Speed-of-light bound analysis exposed kernels that appeared fast but did not perform the intended computation
Targeting Blackwell requires satisfying layout and alignment requirements for tcgen05.mma, a restricted set of supported MMA tile shapes, and explicit warp-specialisation scheduling choices
Standard synthetic GEMM stress tests miss more than 60% of SDC-defective GPUs in a production LLM training fleet

Silent data corruptions are aging-dependent, unit-specific and data-dependent, and are caught by neither ECC nor thermal protection; effective diagnosis requires replay with the exact model, checkpoint, workload and data
Deterministic training cost within 0.01% of step time in production while cutting normalised debug time by 70%; the tool mitigated 40 production incidents

Meta reported hardware failures roughly every 2.78 hours on 16,000-GPU runs with about 1.4% attributed to GPU silent data corruption - cited second-hand inside the OSDI paper and not verified at its own source
Piper reports 2-3.5x higher MFU than X-MoE and an all-to-all at 1.2-9x vendor bandwidth; absolute MFU, accelerator count and machine are not in the abstract
Goodput - the request rate sustainable while meeting both time-to-first-token and inter-token-latency targets - rather than peak tokens per second, is disaggregation's objective

On two L40S GPUs with Qwen2.5-7B at 0.4 req/s, p99 inter-token latency was 169ms collocated vs 29ms disaggregated, while median time-to-first-token was 0.7s collocated vs 2.2s disaggregated; the post states its collocated baseline was not the strongest configuration
On one 8-GPU MI300X node with Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 at 8 req/s, 73 of 100 requests met a 1s TTFT and 50ms ITL target disaggregated vs 30 of 100 collocated - about 2.4x goodput on the same hardware
Llama-3.1-70B in BF16 holds 320 KiB of KV cache per token, so a 10k-token prompt is about 3 GB, about 65ms to transfer at 400 Gb/s before overhead, paid entirely in time-to-first-token
H-Spec removes the drafter-side KV cache by reusing target KV in place, reporting 5.0-13.3% higher mean accepted length and 5.3-12.6% lower batch-1 inter-token latency over an unnamed best baseline
A paged-attention kernel written entirely in Triton was raised from 19.7% to 105.9% of an unnamed state of the art on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs
